oneLiner.zh-TW: 軟體的成分表，列出產品用了哪些元件。
oneLiner.en: An ingredients list for software: which components a product uses.

points.zh-TW: 記錄每個元件的名稱、版本、來源與相依關係。
points.en: It records each component's name, version, source and dependencies.

points.zh-TW: 必須是電腦能自動讀取的格式，手打的 Excel 清單嚴格來說不算。
points.en: It must be machine-readable; a hand-typed spreadsheet doesn't strictly count.

points.zh-TW: 軟體每次改版，都應該重新產生一份。
points.en: It should be regenerated with every release.

why.zh-TW: 某個元件爆出漏洞時，能快速找出哪些產品受影響。歐盟網路韌性法已要求產品製造商提供 SBOM。
why.en: When a component turns out to be vulnerable, it shows which products are affected. The EU Cyber Resilience Act requires manufacturers to provide one.

further.name: iThome：CISA 聯合多國更新 SBOM 最低要素

oneLiner.zh-TW: 每個公開漏洞的「身分證字號」。
oneLiner.en: The ID number for each publicly disclosed vulnerability.

points.zh-TW: 格式是「CVE-年份-流水號」，例如 CVE-2021-44228。
points.en: The format is CVE-year-number, for example CVE-2021-44228.

points.zh-TW: 由 MITRE 在 1999 年建立，現在由美國 CISA 贊助。
points.en: MITRE launched the program in 1999; the US agency CISA now sponsors it.

points.zh-TW: CVE 只負責命名，不代表嚴重程度；嚴重程度要看 CVSS。
points.en: A CVE only names a flaw; severity comes from CVSS.

why.zh-TW: 廠商公告、掃描工具和新聞都用同一個編號，大家才能確定講的是同一個漏洞。
why.en: Vendor advisories, scanners and news all use the same ID, so everyone knows they mean the same flaw.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 漏洞嚴重程度的分數，從 0 到 10 分。
oneLiner.en: A severity score for vulnerabilities, from 0 to 10.

points.zh-TW: 分數越高越嚴重：9.0 以上是「重大」，7.0 到 8.9 是「高」。
points.en: Higher is worse: 9.0 and up is critical, 7.0 to 8.9 is high.

points.zh-TW: 由 FIRST 組織維護，目前版本是 2023 年 11 月發布的 4.0 版。
points.en: FIRST maintains it; the current version, 4.0, came out in November 2023.

points.zh-TW: 分數不考慮你的使用環境，也不一定反映漏洞是否已被利用。
points.en: The score doesn't account for your environment and may not reflect whether a flaw is being exploited.

why.zh-TW: 漏洞多到修不完時，分數是排定先後的參考之一。但已遭利用的漏洞，即使分數不高也該優先處理：本週的 Outlook 零時差漏洞只有 6.5 分，卻已遭實際攻擊。
why.en: When there are too many flaws to fix at once, the score helps set priorities. But exploited flaws come first even with a modest score: this week's Outlook zero-day scored only 6.5 yet was already under attack.

term.zh-TW: KEV 已知遭利用漏洞清單

oneLiner.zh-TW: 美國政府整理的「已確認遭實際攻擊」漏洞清單。
oneLiner.en: The US government's list of vulnerabilities confirmed to be exploited in real attacks.

points.zh-TW: 由美國 CISA 維護，在 2021 年 11 月推出。
points.en: CISA maintains it; it launched in November 2021.

points.zh-TW: 只收錄有可靠證據顯示已遭利用的 CVE，並訂出美國聯邦機構的修補期限。
points.en: It lists only CVEs with reliable evidence of exploitation and sets patch deadlines for US federal agencies.

points.zh-TW: 清單偏保守：已被利用、但還沒通報或確認的漏洞不會出現在上面。
points.en: It's conservative: flaws that are exploited but not yet reported or confirmed won't appear.

why.zh-TW: 比起分數高低，「已經被攻擊」是更急迫的訊號，很適合用來決定先修哪一個。
why.en: Being under attack is a more urgent signal than a high score, which makes it useful for deciding what to fix first.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 廠商還來不及修補，就已經被攻擊者利用的漏洞。
oneLiner.en: A flaw attackers exploit before the vendor can patch it.

points.zh-TW: 因為還沒有修補程式，防毒軟體等工具也可能認不出這種攻擊。
points.en: With no patch yet, antivirus and similar tools may not recognize the attack.

points.zh-TW: 漏洞公開並推出修補後，就稱為 n-day 漏洞；沒有更新的系統仍然有風險。
points.en: Once disclosed and patched, it's called an n-day; unpatched systems remain at risk.

points.zh-TW: 漏洞、攻擊程式、攻擊是三件事：漏洞是缺陷，攻擊程式是利用它的程式碼，攻擊是實際動手。
points.en: Vulnerability, exploit and attack differ: the flaw, the code that uses it, and the act of using it.

why.zh-TW: 修補程式一推出就要盡快安裝。本週 Outlook 和 Chrome 都出現已遭利用的零時差漏洞。
why.en: Install patches as soon as they ship. This week both Outlook and Chrome had exploited zero-days.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 不直接攻擊你，而是攻擊你使用的套件、工具或建置流程。
oneLiner.en: Instead of attacking you directly, attackers compromise the libraries, tools or build processes you rely on.

points.zh-TW: 上游一個熱門套件被入侵，可能自動擴散到下游上千家企業。
points.en: One compromised popular library upstream can spread automatically to thousands of organizations downstream.

points.zh-TW: 它和廣義的第三方風險不同，是把軟體本身當成散布惡意程式的管道。
points.en: Unlike broader third-party risk, it uses the software itself to deliver malware.

points.zh-TW: 維持一份即時更新的 SBOM，是常見的防護基礎。
points.en: Keeping an up-to-date SBOM is a common first line of defense.

why.zh-TW: 現代軟體大量依賴外部套件。Linux 基金會的調查中，60% 受訪者表示 AI 程式工具增加了外部相依套件。
why.en: Modern software leans heavily on outside packages. In a Linux Foundation survey, 60% said AI coding tools have added more external dependencies.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 用特製的文字，讓 AI 不照原本的指示做事。
oneLiner.en: Crafted text that makes an AI stop following its original instructions.

points.zh-TW: 可以直接輸入給 AI，也可以藏在 AI 讀取的網頁、郵件或文件裡。
points.en: It can be typed straight into the AI, or hidden in web pages, emails or documents the AI reads.

points.zh-TW: 一旦成功，AI 可能洩漏機密、外傳資料，或透過工具做出有害的動作。
points.en: If it works, the AI may leak secrets, send data out, or take harmful actions through its tools.

points.zh-TW: 它在 OWASP 2025 年版的 LLM 應用十大風險中排名第一，只靠系統提示的限制無法可靠阻擋。
points.en: It's ranked first in OWASP's 2025 Top 10 for LLM applications, and system-prompt rules alone don't reliably stop it.

why.zh-TW: 越來越多工具會讓 AI 讀外部內容並自動執行動作。本站若導入 AI 摘要，也會因此保留人工審核再發布。
why.en: More tools let AI read outside content and act on it automatically. That's why, if this site adopts AI summaries, a human will still review them before publishing.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 事故結束後，整理發生經過與改善措施的報告。
oneLiner.en: A write-up after an incident: what happened and what will change.

points.zh-TW: 重點是找出促成事故的原因，而不是追究個人或團隊，稱為「不究責」的檢討。
points.en: The aim is to find what contributed to the incident without blaming any person or team; this is called a blameless postmortem.

points.zh-TW: 這種文化源自醫療與航空業，把每次錯誤視為強化系統的機會。
points.en: The culture comes from healthcare and aviation, where every mistake is a chance to strengthen the system.

points.zh-TW: Google 的 SRE 做法強調高階主管積極參與，帶頭示範。
points.en: Google's SRE practice stresses active participation by senior management.

why.zh-TW: 事後檢討通常會說明根本原因與預防措施，是判斷服務商可靠度的重要資料。本站的事件卡片會追蹤它是否發布。
why.en: A postmortem usually explains the root cause and prevention steps, which helps judge a provider's reliability. Our event cards track whether one has been published.

term.zh-TW: CI/CD 持續整合與持續交付

oneLiner.zh-TW: 讓程式碼從修改到上線，自動完成整合、測試與發布的流程。
oneLiner.en: An automated path that takes code changes through integration, testing and release.

points.zh-TW: CI（持續整合）：自動且頻繁地把程式碼變更合併到共用的程式庫，並自動測試。
points.en: CI: automatically and frequently merging code changes into a shared repository, with automated tests.

points.zh-TW: CD 有兩種：持續交付停在正式上線之前，持續部署則會自動發布到正式環境。
points.en: CD comes in two forms: continuous delivery stops short of production, while continuous deployment releases automatically.

points.zh-TW: 要選哪一種，取決於團隊對風險的容忍度。
points.en: Which one to choose depends on the team's risk tolerance.

why.zh-TW: 本站就是例子：推送到 main 之後，GitHub Actions 自動檢查資料與建置，Netlify 自動部署上線。
why.en: This site is an example: pushing to main makes GitHub Actions check the data and build, and Netlify deploys automatically.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 把資安融入開發與維運的每個階段，而不是最後才檢查。
oneLiner.en: Building security into every stage of development and operations instead of checking at the end.

points.zh-TW: 核心原則是「左移」：把資安檢查提早到設計、寫程式與建置階段。
points.en: Its core principle is shifting left: moving security checks earlier, into design, coding and build.

points.zh-TW: 資安測試會整合進 CI/CD 流程中自動執行。
points.en: Security tests run automatically inside the CI/CD pipeline.

points.zh-TW: 資安是開發、資安與維運團隊的共同責任。
points.en: Security becomes a shared responsibility across development, security and operations.

why.zh-TW: 越早發現問題，修正越容易、成本越低。Linux 基金會的調查中，58% 受訪者表示交付速度已快到資安審查跟不上。
why.en: Problems are easier and cheaper to fix the earlier they're found. In a Linux Foundation survey, 58% said delivery now outpaces security review.

term.zh-TW: SAST／DAST 應用程式安全測試

oneLiner.zh-TW: 兩種找程式漏洞的方法：一個看原始碼，一個測執行中的程式。
oneLiner.en: Two ways to find app vulnerabilities: one reads the source code, the other tests the running app.

points.zh-TW: SAST（靜態測試）在程式執行前分析原始碼，寫程式時就能提早發現問題。
points.en: SAST (static testing) analyzes source code before the app runs, catching problems while code is written.

points.zh-TW: DAST（動態測試）測試執行中的程式，能找出只有實際運作時才出現的問題。
points.en: DAST (dynamic testing) probes the running app and finds issues that only show up at runtime.

points.zh-TW: 兩者互補，不是二選一。
points.en: They complement each other; it isn't either-or.

why.zh-TW: SAST 是「左移」的實際做法之一：整合進開發工具和 CI/CD 後，每次提交程式碼都會自動掃描。
why.en: SAST is one practical way to shift left: built into editors and CI/CD, it scans every commit automatically.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 登入時除了密碼，還要用另一種方式證明是你。
oneLiner.en: Proving it's you with something beyond a password when you sign in.

points.zh-TW: 即使密碼被偷或被猜到，MFA 仍能擋下對方登入。
points.en: Even if a password is stolen or guessed, MFA can still stop the sign-in.

points.zh-TW: 並非所有 MFA 都一樣：美國 CISA 把抗網路釣魚的 MFA（例如 FIDO／WebAuthn）稱為「黃金標準」。
points.en: Not all MFA is equal: the US agency CISA calls phishing-resistant MFA, such as FIDO/WebAuthn, the gold standard.

points.zh-TW: 暫時做不到時，CISA 建議至少採用「數字比對」，避免使用者被大量推播轟炸而誤按同意。
points.en: Where that isn't possible yet, CISA recommends number matching so users aren't worn down into approving a flood of push prompts.

why.zh-TW: 服務中斷時常出現假冒「請重新登入」的釣魚信。抗網路釣魚的 MFA 會綁定真正的網域，被騙走的登入資訊無法拿到假網站使用。
why.en: Outages often bring fake "sign in again" phishing. Phishing-resistant MFA is bound to the real domain, so captured credentials can't be replayed on a fake site.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 不因為「在公司網路裡」就信任，每次存取都要驗證。
oneLiner.en: Never trusting a request just because it's inside the network; verifying every access.

points.zh-TW: 口號是「永不信任，持續驗證」（never trust, always verify）。
points.en: The motto is never trust, always verify.

points.zh-TW: 每個存取請求都要經過身分驗證與授權，而且只給完成工作所需的最小權限。
points.en: Every request is authenticated and authorized, and access is limited to the minimum the task needs.

points.zh-TW: 美國 NIST 在 2020 年 8 月發布 SP 800-207，為零信任架構提供正式定義。
points.en: In August 2020, NIST published SP 800-207, giving zero trust architecture a formal definition.

why.zh-TW: 雲端與遠端工作讓「公司內網」的邊界越來越模糊。零信任假設入侵難免發生，在設計上讓損害範圍盡量縮小。
why.en: Cloud and remote work blur the old network perimeter. Zero trust assumes breaches will happen and is designed to keep the damage small.

oneLiner.zh-TW: SSO 讓你登入一次就能用多個系統；OAuth 讓 App 不拿你的密碼也能取得授權。
oneLiner.en: SSO lets you sign in once for many apps; OAuth lets an app get permission without your password.

points.zh-TW: SSO（單一登入）：向身分提供者驗證一次，就能使用多個應用程式。
points.en: SSO (single sign-on): authenticate once with an identity provider and use many apps.

points.zh-TW: OAuth 2.0 是「授權」協定：讓一個 App 取得你在另一個服務上的有限權限，而不需要你的密碼。
points.en: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization protocol: it gives one app limited access to your data in another service without your password.

points.zh-TW: OAuth 本身不負責確認「你是誰」；要做登入驗證，應使用建立在 OAuth 之上的 OpenID Connect。
points.en: OAuth doesn't confirm who you are; for sign-in, use OpenID Connect, which is built on top of OAuth.

why.zh-TW: 「用 Google 帳號登入」背後就是 OpenID Connect。把 OAuth 誤當成登入驗證來用，是常見的設計風險。
why.en: "Sign in with Google" runs on OpenID Connect. Using OAuth alone as a login mechanism is a common design risk.

term.zh-TW: SLA／SLO 服務水準協議與目標

oneLiner.zh-TW: SLO 是內部訂的可靠度目標；SLA 是對客戶的承諾，做不到要補償。
oneLiner.en: An SLO is an internal reliability target; an SLA is a promise to customers, with compensation if it's missed.

points.zh-TW: SLI 是量測值，例如在 300 毫秒內回應的請求比例。
points.en: An SLI is the measurement, such as the share of requests answered within 300 ms.

points.zh-TW: SLO 是 SLI 要達到的目標值或範圍。
points.en: An SLO is the target value or range that the SLI must meet.

points.zh-TW: SLA 是對客戶的承諾，沒達到通常要提供服務抵免或退款。
points.en: An SLA is a promise to customers; missing it usually means service credits or refunds.

why.zh-TW: SLA 決定服務中斷時的補償方式。SLA 通常比內部 SLO 寬鬆，保留緩衝：Google 的說明範例中，SLO 是 99.5%，SLA 是 99%。
why.en: The SLA decides what happens when a service goes down. It's usually looser than the internal SLO to leave a buffer: in Google's example, the SLO is 99.5% and the SLA is 99%.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 發生資安或系統事故時，有計畫地偵測、控制、復原與檢討。
oneLiner.en: Handling a security or system incident with a plan: detect, contain, recover and learn.

points.zh-TW: 美國 NIST SP 800-61 第 2 版把流程分成四個階段：準備、偵測與分析、圍堵／根除／復原、事後活動。
points.en: Revision 2 of NIST SP 800-61 splits the process into four phases: preparation; detection and analysis; containment, eradication and recovery; and post-incident activity.

points.zh-TW: 準備階段最重要：事前訂好政策、角色分工，並定期演練。
points.en: Preparation matters most: set policies and roles in advance, and practice regularly.

points.zh-TW: 如果平常用的電子郵件或通訊系統也受影響，需要事先備妥其他聯絡管道。
points.en: If email or chat systems are affected too, you need other ways to communicate, arranged in advance.

why.zh-TW: Microsoft 365 斷線就是提醒：當 Outlook 和 Teams 同時停擺，團隊要用什麼聯絡？事故應變計畫要事先回答這個問題。
why.en: The Microsoft 365 outage is a reminder: if Outlook and Teams go down together, how does the team stay in touch? An incident response plan answers that ahead of time.

term.zh-TW: VEX 漏洞可利用性聲明

oneLiner.zh-TW: 告訴客戶「這個漏洞到底有沒有影響我們產品」的標準化聲明。
oneLiner.en: A standard statement telling customers whether a known vulnerability actually affects a product.

points.zh-TW: 狀態有四種：不受影響、受影響、已修正、調查中。
points.en: There are four statuses: not affected, affected, fixed and under investigation.

points.zh-TW: 標示「不受影響」時，必須說明理由。
points.en: A not-affected status must come with a justification.

points.zh-TW: 它源自 SBOM：清單列出的元件有漏洞，不代表產品真的能被攻擊，VEX 用來補上這段資訊。
points.en: It grew out of SBOMs: a listed component having a flaw doesn't mean the product is exploitable, and VEX fills that gap.

why.zh-TW: 少了 VEX，客戶拿 SBOM 一掃就會冒出大量漏洞警告。VEX 能減少這些干擾，讓雙方把力氣花在真正受影響的地方。
why.en: Without VEX, scanning an SBOM can flood customers with vulnerability alerts. VEX cuts that noise so both sides can focus on what's really affected.

oneLiner.zh-TW: 把檔案加密鎖住，要求付贖金才解鎖的惡意程式。
oneLiner.en: Malware that encrypts files and demands a ransom to unlock them.

points.zh-TW: 美國 CISA 的定義：一種把裝置上的檔案加密，讓檔案和依賴它們的系統無法使用的惡意程式。
points.en: CISA defines it as malware that encrypts files on a device, making them and the systems that rely on them unusable.

points.zh-TW: 「雙重勒索」是攻擊者先偷走資料再加密，威脅不付錢就公開資料。
points.en: In double extortion, attackers steal data before encrypting it and threaten to publish it unless paid.

points.zh-TW: 因此即使有備份能還原系統，資料外洩的風險依然存在。
points.en: So even when backups restore the systems, the risk of the data leaking remains.

why.zh-TW: 勒索軟體事件應同時當成資料外洩事件處理，而不只是系統停擺；英國 NCSC 也建議假設資料可能已被竊取。
why.en: Treat a ransomware incident as a data breach, not just an outage; the UK's NCSC also advises assuming data may have been stolen.
